title: A Classroom Investigation
paragraphs: A class was investigating how writers turn observations into evidence. The teacher supplied a folder of short accounts and asked the students to look beyond their first impressions. Each account described a particular situation, but the collection raised questions that could apply more widely.

The group began by reading the following accounts without adding explanations of its own. The weaver stretched threads across the loom. We kept the flour in a sealed canister. The report included a figure for the number of daily visitors. The final digit of the code is seven.

It then considered a second group of accounts, looking for both similarities and differences. The clerk checked the address before sorting the mail. The online map was a convenience for visitors planning their route. A multitude of stars appeared above the dark valley. The awards ceremony began with a welcome from the principal.

The class finished by comparing its first impressions with its later interpretations. Some ideas had survived closer examination; others needed to be revised. The students kept the original details visible so that future readers could judge for themselves. They understood that a convincing explanation should connect the evidence clearly while leaving room for questions the records could not answer.

targets.definition: a machine or frame used for weaving cloth
a firm container used for holding or storing something
a number representing an amount or measurement
any one of the numerals from zero to nine
a worker who keeps records or performs routine office tasks
something that makes a task easier or saves effort
a very large number of people or things
a formal event performed according to an established pattern
